newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Rao rattles India, market seen lower.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Rao rattles India, market seen lower.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were marked sharply lower on Thursday after Bombay fell on news former Prime Minister Narasimha Rao would face charges on forgery and is under investigation on two other charges.
"For any market, the potential arrest of a former Prime Minister is a worrying event," said a broker.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index fell 0.97 points, or 1.43 percent to 67.02 points, a premium of 11.29 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 36.87 points to 3,307.05.
Indian GDRs are now down over 21 percent in the quarter.
"There was some bargain hunting in the afternoon, but not a great deal. There is nothing to lift this market and with the State Bank of India issue most people are holding off," said a trader.
IPCL fell after chairman K.G. Ramanathan told shareholders on first half 1996/7 net profit would be 2.2 billion rupees, less than the 3.0 billion net profit forecast by most analysts.
The GDR closed off 75 cents at $9.50/$10.50.
The Capel Korea Index rose 0.66 points 0.95 percent to 70.52 points, a premium of 30.14 percent over the local market which is closed.

Taiwan continued its rally on the back of the local market with the Capel Taiwan Index rose 1.34 points 1.52 percent to 89.29 points a premium of 2.82 percent over the local market after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 69.65 points or 1.08 percent to finish at 6,508.17.
